input.reasoning:
Backlog totals 81 story points across 8 tasks. No historical velocity/actuals exist for this team, so I used industry-typical hours-per-point (6-10 hrs/point blended across roles depending on task type) and split effort by role based on task nature (backend-heavy, frontend-heavy, QA, infra). Team capacity: Backend 1.5 FTE (~2,340 hrs/quarter), Frontend 1.0 FTE (~1,560 hrs/quarter), QA 0.6 FTE (~936 hrs/quarter), DevOps 0.4 FTE (~624 hrs/quarter) assuming a ~13-week (1 quarter) delivery window at ~40hr/week per FTE minus overhead (~120 hrs/month/FTE effective). Given DevOps is only 0.4 FTE, PW-1 (CI/staging) and later infra support consume a large share of that thin capacity, flagged as a risk. Legacy data migration (PW-8, 21 points) is the largest and riskiest item, split across Backend + QA + DevOps. Payment integration (PW-7) and RBAC (PW-4) are also large.

Hours were allocated per task by estimating effort per role:
- PW-1 (CI/staging, 5pt): DevOps-led, some Backend support.
- PW-2 (Design system, 8pt): Frontend-led.
- PW-3 (Registration/login, 8pt): Backend-led with Frontend + QA.
- PW-4 (RBAC, 13pt): Backend-led, Frontend + QA support.
- PW-5 (Dashboard, 8pt): Frontend-led, Backend API support, QA.
- PW-6 (Invoice list/detail, 5pt): Frontend + Backend, QA.
- PW-7 (Payment integration, 13pt): Backend-led (webhooks/reconciliation are backend-heavy), QA, some DevOps for infra/monitoring.
- PW-8 (Data migration, 21pt): Backend-heavy scripting/ETL, DevOps for environment/cutover, QA for validation.

Total hours per role were summed and rates applied exactly per the rate card. Non-labour costs added for staging/cloud infra, Stripe fees/sandbox, and a data migration tooling/environment cost given the scale (400k records, 2M invoice lines) and typical one-off migration tooling/licensing needs.

Scenarios: P50 is the base estimate as built. P75 (likely) adds ~15% contingency for integration/testing overruns typical in payment and migration work. P90 (worst case) adds ~30% to account for RBAC complexity, Stripe reconciliation edge cases, and legacy schema surprises in migration.

Reductions identified: defer design system polish (theming tokens) to later phase, reduce QA scope on lower-priority invoice view by relying on shared test cases from dashboard work, and negotiate a phased/partial data migration (e.g., migrate active accounts first, defer historical/inactive records) to cut initial migration hours.

nonLabourLines.description: Cloud infrastructure & staging environment (CI/CD, hosting) - first quarter
Stripe integration sandbox/testing fees and webhook monitoring tooling
Legacy data migration tooling/licensing (ETL tools, temporary Oracle connectivity)
Contingency buffer for third-party API changes / migration data cleansing

assumptions: No historical actuals/velocity data exist for this team; estimates are based on typical industry hours-per-story-point benchmarks, not project-specific history.
1 story point is assumed to equate to roughly 6-9 blended engineering hours depending on task complexity and role mix.

Delivery window assumed to be approximately one quarter (13 weeks); FTE capacity figures are derived from this window (Backend ~2,340 hrs, Frontend ~1,560 hrs, QA ~936 hrs, DevOps ~624 hrs), though actual allocation is well below max capacity to leave room for other concurrent work and non-project overhead.

DevOps Engineer is staffed at only 0.4 FTE, which is thin relative to the CI/staging setup (PW-1), payment infra, and migration cutover support all competing for this same limited pool of hours; this is a scheduling risk.
Legacy data migration (PW-8) is treated as the highest-risk item due to unknown legacy schema quality; hours may increase materially once schema profiling is done.
Payment provider integration (PW-7) assumes Stripe (not a custom PSP), reducing integration complexity versus a bespoke gateway.
QA Engineer at 0.6 FTE is assumed to focus testing effort on Urgent/High priority items first, with lighter regression coverage on Medium priority items (PW-2, PW-6).
Non-labour costs are rough order-of-magnitude estimates for cloud infra, Stripe sandbox fees, and migration tooling; actual vendor quotes were not available.
Priority breakdown totals are approximate allocations of labour + non-labour costs mapped to the priority of the dominant tasks in each band.

reductions.description: Defer full theming tokens/advanced design system polish (PW-2) to a later phase, delivering only core components (buttons, forms, tables, dialogs) now.
reductions.effect: Reduces Frontend Developer hours on PW-2 by ~70 hours.

reductions.description: Phase the legacy data migration (PW-8): migrate active customer accounts and recent invoices first, defer historical/inactive records to a follow-up project phase.
reductions.effect: Reduces Backend, QA, and DevOps hours allocated to PW-8 by roughly 35%, plus reduces migration tooling non-labour cost.

reductions.description: Reduce dedicated QA regression coverage on Medium-priority Invoice list/detail view (PW-6), relying on reused test cases from the Dashboard (PW-5) work.
reductions.effect: Cuts QA Engineer hours on PW-6 by ~30 hours.

reductions.description: Delay non-critical DevOps monitoring/alerting setup for Stripe webhooks until post-launch stabilization sprint.
reductions.effect: Removes the Stripe monitoring tooling non-labour line item from initial budget.
